tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For Assessment Year (AY) 2016-17, the Income-tax return filed by the Company was selected for tax assessment by the Income-tax department. The Assistant Commissioner of Income-tax- Circle 12(3)(2), Mumbai, completed the assessment and passed an assessment order under Section 143 of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Aggrieved with the order, the Company challenged the same before the Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeal) by preferring an appeal. The litigation is with regard to various transfer pricing adjustments made, disallowances of deductions/expenses claimed, etc. As of now, the case is pending disposal.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner of Income-tax- Circle 12(3)(2), Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: The case is pending for disposal with Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals).

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For the Assessment Year (AY) 2017-18, the Income-tax return filed by the Company was selected for tax assessment by the Income-tax department. The Tax authority at the National Faceless Assessment Centre, Income-tax department, New Delhi, completed the assessment and passed an assessment order under Section 143 of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Aggrieved with the order, the Company challenged the matter before the Commissioner of Income-tax (Appeal) by preferring an appeal. The litigation is with regard to various transfer pricing adjustments made, disallowances of deductions/expenses claimed, etc. As of now, the case is pending disposal.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Tax Authority at the National Faceless Assessment Centre, Income-tax department, New Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The case is pending for disposal with Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals).

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received an assessment order pertaining to Income Tax demand of Rs. 142.07 Crores on account of various transfer pricing adjustments made, disallowances of deductions/expenses claimed, etc. The Company will file a rectification application with the Income Tax Department seeking correction of certain errors in the said order, consequent to which the demand amount should stand substantially reduced. The Company will also pursue an appeal against the order under the applicable laws. The above matter is in the normal course of business and the Company expects a favourable outcome considering the factual and legal grounds pertaining to the matter. Further, it is not likely to have a material impact on financials or operations of the Company.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Tax Authority at the National Faceless Assessment Centre, Income-tax department, New Delhi
tax_litigation.status: The case is pending for disposal with Income Tax Appellate Tribunal.

timeline.summary: Marico Limited updated the webcast link for its investor/analyst conference call on May 5, 2026, at 5:30 p.m. (IST), led by **Vinay M A**.
Marico reported Q4FY26 consolidated PAT of ₹408 Cr on revenue of ₹3,333 Cr and recommended a ₹4/share final dividend.
Harsh C Mariwala, on behalf of Marico’s promoters and PAC, declared no new encumbrances on shares as of **April 3, 2026**, excluding those already disclosed.
Marico’s Management will attend 360 ONE Capital’s 16th Annual One-on-One Investor Conference in Mumbai on May 29, 2026.
Marico announced its entry into the hair cleansing segment with the launch of Parachute Advansed Protein Shampoo.
